Laser Tube Cutting Example 1: Multi-Passage Transfer for Laser Tube Cutting Selection objective: separate assist-gas, clamping-air, and coolant circuits Engineering Requirement A rotating cutting or clamping assembly may need several independent fluid paths without twisting external hoses. The correct passage count depends on the machine circuit diagram; oxygen, nitrogen, compressed air, and coolant must not be combined unless the machine design explicitly permits it. Selection itemTypical questionBegapunk direction PassagesHow many independent circuits cross the rotating interface?Choose the same number of isolated passages, with spare capacity only when justified. Pressure and mediaWhat are normal and peak pressure for each circuit?Confirm every medium and pressure separately before model approval. SpeedContinuous rotation or intermittent indexing?Use continuous-duty speed, not only peak RPM. MountingThreaded body or flange pattern?Verify bolt pattern, port orientation, and available envelope in CAD. Candidate Products BP-2P-0001 can be evaluated for two low-pressure circuits. Three or more circuits require a matching multi-passage model or a custom review. The machine builder must confirm gas compatibility and applicable safety requirements. A standard indoor pneumatic model should not be assumed suitable for offshore service. Input requiredWhy it matters Media and concentrationDetermines seal and metal compatibility. Pressure, RPM, and duty cycleDefines the combined pressure-speed operating point. Temperature rangeAffects elastomer selection and dimensional clearances. Corrosion or test standardDefines coating, material, and validation requirements. Maintenance intervalInfluences bearing protection and serviceability. Any corrosive or safety-critical application requires drawing review, material confirmation, and an agreed validation plan. Request Custom Feasibility Review CNC & Indexing Machinery Example 3: CAD Fit Check Before CNC Installation Selection objective: verify bore, flange, ports, and surrounding clearance Engineering Requirement Even when pressure and RPM are suitable, installation can fail because of bolt-pattern mismatch, insufficient hollow-bore clearance, hose interference, or rigid piping loads. A CAD fit check reduces dimensional risk before production. CheckRequired confirmation Hollow boreClearance around the shaft, drawbar, cable, or tooling. EnvelopeBody diameter, total length, and service access. MountingBolt circle, thread specification, depth, and locating feature. Ports and hosesFitting size, bend radius, and freedom from external load. Operating pointMedia, normal pressure, peak pressure, RPM, and duty cycle. Candidate Product BP-2P-30-0001 provides a 30 mm hollow-bore catalog option. Download or request the current drawing and confirm all interfaces in the machine assembly before ordering. h1: Frequently Asked Questions
body: Frequently Asked Questions Everything you need to know about Begapunk rotary joints — from selection to installation. ? General Questions What is a rotary joint / rotary union? ▼ A rotary joint (also called rotary union or swivel joint) is a precision mechanical device used to transfer fluid — air, water, oil, coolant, or steam — from a stationary source to a rotating destination, or vice versa. Begapunk manufactures single-passage and multi-passage rotary unions for industrial automation, CNC machining, laser cutting, packaging, and other rotating machinery applications. What is the difference between a rotary joint and a rotary union? ▼ There is no technical difference — the terms are used interchangeably in the industry. "Rotary union" is more common in North America, while "rotary joint" is widely used in Europe and Asia. Both refer to the same device: a mechanical seal assembly that transfers fluid between stationary and rotating components. ★ Product Selection What parameters do I need to specify for a quote? ▼ The key parameters are: Media type: Air, water, coolant, hydraulic oil, steam, or other Number of passages: 1-in-1-out, 2-in-2-out, 3-in-3-out, or custom multi-passage Max pressure: In bar or psi Max speed: In RPM Connection type: Threaded (NPT/BSP) or flange mount Mounting space constraints: Any dimensional limitations A machine drawing is helpful but not required. Begapunk aims to respond promptly to complete technical inquiries. Response time depends on the application complexity and the information provided. What media can pass through a Begapunk rotary joint? ▼ Our standard rotary joints handle: compressed air, water, water-soluble coolant, hydraulic oil (up to ISO VG 32), and thermal oil. The PTFE composite seals are compatible with most common industrial fluids. For steam, aggressive chemicals, or food-grade applications, please contact our engineering team for material recommendations. What is the maximum pressure and speed? ▼ Our product range covers a wide performance spectrum: Standard models: Up to 1 MPa (10 bar / 145 psi) and 500 RPM Heavy-duty models: Up to 10 MPa (100 bar) and 2,000 RPM High-speed models: Up to 10,000 RPM (air only, balanced seal design) For requirements beyond these specifications, we design custom solutions. Send us your parameters for a feasibility assessment. Can I pass multiple media through the same rotary joint? ▼ Yes — that's exactly what our multi-passage rotary unions are designed for. Each passage has independent seals and isolated flow paths, so there is zero cross-contamination between channels. Common examples: 3-channel: Oxygen + Nitrogen + Coolant in laser tube cutting machines 2-channel: Compressed air + Vacuum in packaging machinery 6-channel: Hydraulic oil + Cooling water + Grease in wind turbine pitch systems What materials are used in Begapunk rotary joints? ▼ Material selection depends on the application: Body: AL6061 aluminum (lightweight, anodized blue), Grade 45 carbon steel, 304 stainless steel, or 316 stainless steel Shaft: Grade 45 carbon steel, 304 SS, or 316 SS Seals: PTFE composite (standard), carbon fiber, graphite, or ceramic Custom materials available upon request for corrosive environments, high temperatures, or food-grade applications. ✉ Custom Orders & Delivery Do you offer custom rotary joint designs? ▼ Yes — custom design is our specialty. Our engineering team will work with you to design a rotary joint for any number of passages, pressure, speed, mounting type, and material. Process: You send complete requirements → Begapunk reviews the application and responds based on its complexity and the information provided. Upon order confirmation → We provide a free 3D STEP file for fit verification You approve the design → We manufacture (typically 3 weeks) Inspection scope confirmed → Order released for shipment Start your custom inquiry → What is the minimum order quantity (MOQ)? ▼ Standard models: 1 piece. Custom designs: typically 5–10 pieces for the first order. We understand the need for prototypes and samples — there is no penalty for small orders. How long is delivery? ▼ Delivery times depend on the product type: Standard models (in stock): 7–10 days worldwide via air freight Custom designs: 3 weeks production + 5–7 days shipping DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) terms available — we handle customs clearance and import duties for you. What warranty do you offer? ▼ All Begapunk rotary joints carry a 12-month replacement warranty from the date of delivery. The warranty covers material defects and manufacturing defects. If a seal fails within warranty due to a covered defect, we ship a replacement unit immediately — return of the defective unit is not required. See our Terms of Service for full details. Are rotary joints tested before shipment? ▼ Inspection scope, test pressure, and acceptance criteria are defined by the product drawing, order, and approved test plan. Available test records can be requested for the specific project. Do you provide 3D CAD files? ▼ Yes — free of charge. We provide STEP and IGES files for all standard models. For custom designs, we provide 2D drawings for approval before production, and 3D files with the shipment. This allows your mechanical team to verify fit and mounting compatibility before ordering. ⚙ Installation & Maintenance What mounting types are available? ▼ We offer two standard mounting types: Threaded mount: NPT or BSP threads — connect directly to your equipment Flange mount: Bolt-on flange with O-ring face seal — provides a rigid sealed connection; acceptance criteria depend on the application Custom mounting configurations are available. Important: Always use flexible hose connections — never hard-pipe a rotary joint. See our Installation Guide for details. What causes early rotary joint failure? ▼ The most common causes of premature failure are: Hard piping: Rigid connections transfer vibration and misalignment to bearings and seals Side-loading: Hoses under tension or sharp bends apply lateral force to the joint Contamination: Unfiltered media grinds grooves into seal faces — use 25 micron or finer filtration Over-speed / over-pressure: Exceeding rated specifications Rigid anti-rotation: Anti-rotation devices must allow the joint to self-center Following our Installation Guide will prevent most of these issues. Can rotary joints be rebuilt or repaired? ▼ Yes. Most Begapunk rotary joints can be rebuilt using OEM seal kits. Use replacement seals that match the specified material, hardness, geometry, and surface requirements. Non-equivalent seals may cause premature wear or leakage. Contact our support team with your product serial number to order the correct seal kit. What filtration is required? ▼ Begapunk requires fluid filtration to 25 microns or finer for general applications, and 10 microns or finer for high-speed or precision rotary unions. Contaminants larger than the seal gap will embed in the seal material and cause irreversible shaft scoring. Inadequate filtration may void your warranty. Didn't find your answer? Our engineering team is happy to help with your specific application. Contact Us → Get a Quote WhatsApp

title: Rotary Joint Installation Instructions | Begapunk Support
description: Step-by-step installation guide for Begapunk rotary joints and rotary unions. Proper mounting, connections, anti-rotation, filtration, and maintenance.
h1: Installation Instructions
body: Home / Installation Instructions Installation Instructions Proper mounting, connection, and maintenance guidelines for Begapunk rotary joints and rotary unions. Follow these steps to support reliable operation and reduce avoidable leakage risk. 1 Connections 1Use flexible connections. Begapunk rotary joints must always be installed using flexible hose connections. To avoid damage to the bearings, the union needs to find its center during operation. Never hard-pipe either the shaft or the housing. 2Pre-assemble in a vise. Hold the housing of the union in a vise and install the flexible connection before mounting the union to the machine. This prevents twisting during installation. 3Clean and seal threads. Clean female threads and the face of the shaft prior to installation. Use PTFE (Teflon) pipe tape or pipe sealant on NPT threads. NPT threads should be hand-tight plus 1–3 turns to seal. For parallel threads, use appropriate gaskets or O-rings. 4Allow free movement. There should be a slight, kink-free curve in the hose when installed. It is essential that the housing or shaft is allowed to float to compensate for any eccentricity or misalignment. Important: Hard-piping either side will transfer machine vibration and misalignment directly to the bearings and seals, causing premature failure. 2 Anti-Rotation In many applications, the flexible hose connections themselves provide sufficient anti-rotation. For other installations, an external anti-rotation device is required — such as a fork around the fittings, pin, yoke, or bracket. Anti-rotation devices must "float." They should prevent rotation of the stationary side but must not rigidly lock the union in place. The device must allow the union to self-center during operation. Warning: A rigid anti-rotation setup that prevents the union from floating will cause seal wear and leakage within weeks. 3 Filtration To prevent scoring damage to the shaft and seal faces, Begapunk requires fluid filtration to 25 microns or finer for general applications, and 10 microns or finer for high-speed or precision unions. Contaminants larger than the seal gap will embed in the seal material and grind grooves into the shaft face. This damage is irreversible and will cause progressive leakage. Warranty Note: Failure to provide adequate filtration may void your warranty and cause premature failure. 4 Lubrication If your Begapunk rotary joint is equipped with grease fittings (typically on the bearing housing): Use lithium-based grease rated for the operating temperature of your application. Lubricate with no more than two pumps of grease per fitting during routine maintenance. Over-greasing can force grease past the seals and contaminate the fluid path. Refer to your product data sheet for the recommended lubrication interval (typically every 3–6 months for continuous-duty applications). 5 Startup Checklist Verify all connections are tight but not over-torqued. Confirm hoses have a gentle curve — no tension or kinks. Check that the anti-rotation device allows free float. Verify filtration system is active and filter is clean. Start at low speed and pressure, then gradually ramp to operating conditions. Inspect for leaks during the first 30 minutes of operation. 6 Maintenance Monthly: Visual inspection for leaks, hose condition, and anti-rotation clearance. Quarterly: Grease bearings (if fitted), check filter pressure differential, inspect seal faces for wear. Annually: Replace seals if leakage exceeds acceptable limits. Contact Begapunk for OEM seal kits — third-party seals may have incorrect durometer or material. Need a seal kit or have questions? Contact our support team with your product serial number. body: Home › Case Studies › BP-2P-95-0001 Pneumatic Chuck Integration Real Application Case BP-2P-95-0001 Pneumatic Chuck Integration Case Workshop photographs show how BP-2P-95-0001 was positioned in a pneumatic chuck assembly to transfer compressed air from the stationary side toward rotating components. Case Summary ItemDocumented scope ProductBP-2P-95-0001 ApplicationPneumatic chuck assembly MediumCompressed air Integration typeStationary-to-rotating compressed-air connection at the chuck EvidenceTwo workshop photographs showing the visible assembly and connection arrangement Pneumatic chuck integration Connection Detail The close view is the primary installation evidence.
